finding.title: Mirror scheduler's domain/projection tests under test/features/scheduler/domain/projection per AG-5
finding.why: There is no test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/ directory at all — the 4-file domain/projection/ module (overdue_projection.dart, overdue_schedule.dart, overdue_types.dart, projection.dart) is instead tested from files scattered loosely under test/features/scheduler/, including overdue_from_elapsed_study_days_test.dart which sits inside the unrelated data/repositories/ test directory despite importing only domain/projection/projection.dart. A contributor looking for 'the projection tests' at the standard mirrored path won't find them, and a future agent adding coverage for overdue_projection.dart risks not noticing this file already covers related ground.
finding.recommendation: Relocate the projection-only test files under test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/ to match lib/features/scheduler/domain/projection/.
acceptance_criteria: overdue_from_elapsed_study_days_test.dart and the other projection-only test files (e.g. reorder_amnesty_test.dart, collapse_daf_tasks_test.dart if scoped to projection) live under test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/.

finding.title: Populate the scheduler feature barrel (scheduler.dart) with real exports

evidence.quote: // feature. Do NOT import deep paths directly.

finding.why: The entire file is a library declaration plus a comment claiming to be the feature's public surface — it contains zero `export` statements, so importing it gives a consumer nothing usable. Grepping the whole repo confirms no file anywhere imports `features/scheduler/scheduler.dart`; every cross-feature consumer (e.g. lib/core/labels/curriculum_label.dart, lib/core/providers/calendar_providers.dart) is forced into deep imports of internal scheduler files because there is nothing else to import. The same empty-barrel pattern exists in learning.dart and profiles.dart and settings.dart (0 exports each) versus tracks.dart (26 exports, a real barrel) — so Rule 2 is currently unimplementable for scheduler even by a well-intentioned contributor, independent of the separate checker bug (see the awk finding).
finding.recommendation: Either populate scheduler.dart with `export` statements for the types/providers other features legitimately need (services, providers, models used cross-feature) and migrate the deep-import call sites, or formally scope down Rule 2's claim until barrels are built out feature-by-feature.
acceptance_criteria: scheduler.dart exports the symbols currently deep-imported by other features (calendar_program_service.dart, local_calendar_engine.dart, learning_program_service.dart, calendar_program_registry.dart at minimum).
Once check 15 (see companion finding) is fixed, a grep for `features/scheduler/(?!scheduler\.dart)` from outside lib/features/scheduler/ returns zero matches.

finding.title: Split the 5 oversized hand-written scheduler files under the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: scheduler_providers.dart is 1381 lines (3.4x the cap, and the batch HOTSPOT), scheduler_engine.dart is 747, goal_setup_screen.dart is 728 (HOTSPOT), study_day_config_screen.dart is 495, sefaria_ref_matcher.dart is 420. Files this size are slow to review, easy to introduce shotgun-surgery bugs in (the delay-stage date bug and the dead onCompleted chain both hid inside two of these five files), and resist the 1:1 test-mirroring convention (AG-5) since no single test file can reasonably cover a 1381-line source file's behavior space.
finding.recommendation: Extract cohesive chunks per file: scheduler_providers.dart's _buildProjectionTasks/_buildFreshPlan/_applyProgramCalendarOverrides/programCalendarSchedule into domain/services or domain/projection (see companion misplaced-logic finding); scheduler_engine.dart's stage-type processors (_processDelayStage/_processWeeklyStage/_processRollingStage) into their own strategy classes; goal_setup_screen.dart's deadline/pace sections into separate widget files; sefaria_ref_matcher.dart's range-expansion vs fuzzy-matching functions into two files.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 5 files is ≤400 hand-written lines.
A committed line-count check (matching AG-3's stated limit) runs in `make audit` or CI and lists any future violator with its line count.

finding.title: Normalize config.currentDate before delay-stage due-date arithmetic in SchedulerEngine
finding.why: config.currentDate flows in unnormalized: allDailyTasksProvider sets `now = ref.watch(clockProvider)` (a raw timestamp with time-of-day) and _buildFreshPlan passes it straight through generator.generateAll(activeCurricula, now, ...) -> ScheduleConfig(currentDate: date). previousCompletedAt also carries a real time-of-day (completion timestamps are never normalized — confirmed via completion_writer.dart). Duration.inDays truncates toward zero, so when the true calendar-day gap is exactly 1 day but the elapsed wall-clock time is <24h (e.g. item completed at 20:00 five days ago, now it's 02:00 the next calendar day — only 6h elapsed), daysUntilDue computes 0 instead of -1: a chazara item that is genuinely 1+ calendar days overdue is shown in 'due today' (scheduledTasks) instead of 'overdue' (overdueTasks), silently under-reporting overdue-ness by up to a day. This is the same class of bug (R4-1) this codebase has explicitly fixed elsewhere in the very same feature (local_calendar_engine.dart's UTC-midnight handling, goal_setup_screen.dart's daysRemaining guard, and _buildProjectionTasks's pervasive DateUtils.extractLocalDate use) — just missed in the delay-stage path.
finding.recommendation: Normalize both previousCompletedAt/currentCompletedAt and config.currentDate to calendar-date-only (e.g. via DateUtils.extractLocalDate) before computing daysUntilDue in _processDelayStage, matching the pattern already used in _buildProjectionTasks.
acceptance_criteria: New unit test: a delay-stage item whose previous-stage completedAt time-of-day is later than the current query's time-of-day, with a true 1-calendar-day gap, asserts the task lands in overdueTasks (not scheduledTasks).
scheduler_engine_schedule_types_test.dart / scheduler_engine_dni346_test.dart (sibling test files) continue to pass.

finding.title: Move scheduler_providers.dart's projection/plan-building business logic into the domain layer
finding.why: _buildProjectionTasks and _buildFreshPlan are ~200-line pure-ish business-logic functions (amnesty cutoffs, program-vs-self-paced branching, prior-completion filtering) that belong in domain/services or domain/projection — both of which already exist as sibling directories in this exact feature for exactly this purpose. Worse, both functions take `Ref ref` directly as a parameter even though the SAME function signatures already inject `getScopedContent` and `programRepository` as plain callbacks specifically so the logic can be tested without booting Riverpod — the `ref` param undermines that seam (it's used only for one call, `curriculumLabelTextFromRef(ref, curriculum: ...)`, which could equally be injected as a callback like the others). This is why this file is 1381 lines and why testing this logic requires a real ProviderContainer instead of plain unit tests.
finding.recommendation: Extract _buildProjectionTasks/_buildFreshPlan/_applyProgramCalendarOverrides/programCalendarSchedule to a domain/projection or domain/services class; replace the `Ref ref` parameter with a plain `String Function(CurriculumId) trackLabelFor` callback matching the existing DI pattern used for getScopedContent/programRepository.
acceptance_criteria: _buildProjectionTasks and _buildFreshPlan (or their relocated equivalents) take no Ref parameter.
A new domain-layer unit test exercises the amnesty-cutoff and program-vs-self-paced branching logic without a ProviderContainer.
scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart continues to pass unmodified in behavior.
